newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas up in active trade, June and July busie.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas up in active trade, June and July busie.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market traded 525 lots on Tuesday, the third highest volume since the contract started on January 19, with prices rising for most periods.

July was the most active month, with 205 lots traded including 100 in a single trade at the end of the afternoon session, but June also saw 100 lots traded in two deals. Prices in both months were up, with last deals done at 10.35 in June and 10.30 in July, up by 0.050 and 0.025 pence a therm respectively.

"I think it's just an additional player who's bought some decent sized volumes in June and July," said a futures broker. He said he was not sure if there was a completely new player in the market or if it was an "occasional" player coming in after a few days' absence.

Prices in August and September were also stronger, although the volume of trade was not as large. And there was also active business done in April '98, the last month of the contract, where 85 lots traded. The last deal there was done at 12.00 pence a therm, down by a full quarter of a penny and the only month to see a significant downturn in prices.

A futures broker was encouraged by the volume of trade done, even though there are still frequently days when hardly any deals are concluded. "Anything better than nought is good, and anything more than a couple of hundred is something to build on," he said.

There are signs that an increasing number of players are trading spreads between the OTC market and the futures market. "Both markets will help each other," said a broker. "There are good reasons to trade both."
A spokeswoman for the IPE said that the natural gas contract "is now developing its own momentum."
